frames to the next step of the fade-out.
the instrument's fifth byte: bit 3 keeps the pulse width from note to note, the high nibble the release point.
the instrument's vibrato byte: speed in the low nibble, depth in the high.
the instrument's sixth byte: the low nibble picks a pulse program, the high nibble the vibrato's delay.
the instrument's last byte: bit 7 runs a waveform and note program, bit 6 an arpeggio, bit 5 a pitch drop at the note's end, bit 4 the detune, and the low nibble without bit 7 a drum start.
the tick of the note at which its gate is released.
the voice's instrument times 8, an index into the instruments at $3902.
the note the voice plays, 0 to 95, or $FF for a rest.
the tick of a glide's start (pattern byte $FD): the note's length less the glide's delay.

the note the glide goes to.

starts tune A: A times 8 ($FF) indexes the tune's entries ($381B); the tune's transpose ($3822) into the add at $330D; the SID cleared ($33B8), the volume 15, the voices' state cleared, each voice released ($301C = $FE) with its first note at once ($301F = 1), and the tune on.

one frame, while the tune is on ($3017): the volume with the filter mode ($30EE, 0) to $D418, the filter's routing ($30F5) and cutoff (0) to the SID, each voice's shadow registers to the SID; a fade-out step every $3006 frames, the tune stopping at volume 0; at the end of each tick each voice reads on ($31BC), and every frame its effects ($33CE).
the filter mode for $D418's high nibble, which end_music_start clears and nothing else writes: the operand of the lda at $30ED, written at $30B5.
the SID's volume, the operand of the ora at $30EF: 15 at the start, counted down by the fade-out, set by an order list's $FA.
the operand of the lda at $30F4 that goes to $D417, the filter's resonance and routing, set by a pattern's $FE.
silences the three voices (frequency 0) and turns the tune off.

reads the voice's pattern ($F3,x through $382B/$3841, position $F6,x); at its end ($FF) plays it again while $3025 counts, then reads the order list (through $381B, position $F9,x): $FF loops to its start, $FE ends the tune, $FC sets the fade, $FA the volume, $80-$FF a transpose, $70-$7F an instrument offset, $60-$6F a repeat, $50-$5F an arpeggio base, otherwise the next pattern. A pattern's bytes: $FE the filter, $FD a glide, $FC the fade, $E0-$FF a rest of that length, $C0-$DF an instrument, $80-$9F a length, $60-$7F an arpeggio, $FB a tie, below $60 a note.
the adc # whose operand ($330E) adds the tune's transpose to each note; the code from here starts the note with its instrument ($3902).
the tune's transpose, which end_music_start writes into this add; the code from here stores the note and starts it with its instrument: the operand of the adc at $330D, written at $30A5.
sets the test bit and clears the gate of each voice, then zeroes the SID's registers $D400-$D41F.

one frame of a voice's effects: on a new note a glide's set-up, a drum start ($3999, $399D) and the vibrato's ($3907, $3908); then the glide, the vibrato after its delay, the pitch drop at the end of the note (bit 5), the pulse program ($3866), the waveform and note programs ($386F, $3879), the drum's waveform back after its time, and the arpeggio ($3857).
the end-of-note pitch drop, half the step on every other frame; the code from here sets the frequency's high byte lower: the operand of the sbc at $359F, written at $3587, $3598.
the pulse sweep's top limit for the pulse width's high byte, from the program's second byte: the operand of the cmp at $3636, written at $35D6.
the pulse sweep's bottom limit for the pulse width's high byte, from the program's first byte: the operand of the cmp at $3652, written at $35D0.
the waveform program's number, which picks the note program; the code from here reads the voice's note program: the operand of the ldy at $368C, written at $3663.
the note program's step, held in the lda #: added to the note (bit 7 clear) or a note of its own (bit 7 set): the operand of the lda at $36B3, written at $36AB.
the frequency of note A from the tables at $375B (low bytes) and $37BB (high), into the voice's shadow registers.

the ending, called by the boot's script once the war is won ($0398 the winner): sets the machine up ($81BC) and puts the number of months ($0399 tens, $039A units) into the four messages; then, when one person played against the computer, only the screen for that person: the victory ($8050) if the person won, the defeat ($80BF) if the computer did; with two people, or the computer playing both, the victory and then the defeat.

the winner's screen: its colours into colour RAM ($86E4), black border and background, tune 0 ($3000), and the scrolling message for the winner (the Union's at $858A, the Confederacy's at $850E) with the winner's rank from its level ($0380, $86C0) written into it; the raster interrupts on ($831D); then waits ($815D).

the high byte of the winner's rank text victory_screen copies: the high byte of the address of the lda at $80AD, written at $80A8.

the loser's screen: its picture copied into place (screen bytes from $2800 to $6000, colours from $2C00, bitmap from $9000 to $4000, eight kilobytes through the operands at $80FA and $80FD), black border and background, tune 1, and the message for the loser (the Union's at $847B, the Confederacy's at $862D) with the loser's rank written into it; the interrupts on; then waits ($815D).
